cohort: 304,023 women aged 18-44 years in the United States who delivered between October 1, 2019, and September 30, 2020, had singleton deliveries, and completed a birth report in the Ovia Pregnancy mobile app
finding: Compared to the pre-pandemic period, the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a decrease in preterm delivery rates, an increase in home birth rates, and a decrease in the average hospital length of stay post-delivery, with no overall changes in Cesarean section rates.
mod_finding: There were no overall changes in Cesarean section rates between the pre-pandemic and pandemic cohorts.
